audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and First item rendered as Skill while whys[3] and whys[5] both describe Quinn converting and staying ahead; 2+ items rendered as Quinn while whys[6], spikes[3] and the late paragraph all say Tryndamere is the nightmare her kit cannot solve.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Quinn x6, Tryndamere], and Quinn wins 60.05% over 388 games — the strongest win rate in this slice, consistent with owning every lane stage and losing the scaling race.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 5 to Quinn, row 6 to Tryndamere, as one atomic group across both layers, with ratings and phases[6].why brought into line.

audit.why: Quinn levels 1-2, level 3 with the full pattern, first item into roam, Tryndamere late with stacked crit and Undying Rage — right and ordered. Numbers now attached: R is 120s at rank 1 for 5 seconds, Bloodlust 12s, Spinning Slash 650 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction in this lane is absent: Mocking Shout (W) only reduces MOVE SPEED against enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere. Running away in a straight line is what arms it. Quinn's Vault repositions her without ever turning to flee, which is why her disengage beats his chase — nothing on the page said so. Two slot errors also run through the text: Bloodlust is his Q heal, but whys[3], mid, late and wants.foe[0] all call it 'W self-heal'; and the blind is credited with zeroing Spinning Slash, which is ability damage a blind cannot touch.
audit.why: Riot text for W: 'Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' Riot text for Q: 'He can cast Bloodlust to consume his Fury and heal himself.' Riot text for E: 'Tryndamere slices toward a target unit, dealing damage to enemies in his path' — no basic attack involved.
audit.corrected: Back-turned condition written into report[5].t and dontsFull[2].d; Bloodlust reattributed to Q in whys[3] and wants.foe[0]; the blind re-scoped to his crit autos in whys[2] and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Undying Rage's cooldown' with no number, and the advice 'blind his autos, kite it' did not say the one thing that matters — that damage into the 5 seconds is wasted.
audit.why: At 120s on rank 1 it is the longest cooldown in the matchup and the single largest tempo swing; a player who spends burst into it has thrown a full rotation.
audit.corrected: Cooldown, duration and the walk-away instruction stated in breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.why: report[8].t buys early anti-heal, and the missing-interactions file confirms Bloodlust is the sustain that decides extended trades. Plated Steelcaps is also the right boot against a full-crit auto-attacker.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Undying Rage eats your whole burst at 1 HP and full crit answers back. Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10 — end it first.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Blind his autos, kite it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Undying Rage (R): 120s at rank 1, 5 seconds at 1 HP — blind him and kite it out rather than dumping damage into it. - Bloodlust (Q, 12s) is the heal, not his W. - Spinning Slash (E) is the 650-range gap close.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Blind his autos, kite it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Mocking Shout slows you only with your back turned — Vault past him instead of running, and it never applies.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Blind his autos, kite it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Five seconds at 1 HP on a 120s cooldown — walk away, do not feed it damage.

edits.before: Vaulting INTO the fight to feel like an assassin — Vault is your spacing reset, not an engage.
edits.after: Turning your back is what arms Mocking Shout's slow — reposition with Vault, never a straight run.

edits.before: Q-W-E online means you blind the spin to zero, Vault out, and re-mark with Harrier — a free trade he has no answer to pre-fury.
edits.after: Q-W-E online means you blind his crit autos to nothing, Vault out, and re-mark with Harrier — a free trade he cannot answer pre-fury.

edits.before: You convert blind-trades into plates and a shove while his W self-heal can't keep pace with your leap-reset poke.
edits.after: You convert blind-trades into plates and a shove while Bloodlust (Q) cannot heal back your leap-reset poke.

edits.before: Blind (Q) his Spinning Slash spin the moment he engages so his crit autos whiff
edits.after: Blind (Q) him as Spinning Slash lands so the crit autos that follow it whiff

edits.before: Stack fury early so his passive crit and W self-heal let him outsustain your pokes
edits.after: Stack Fury early so his passive crit and Bloodlust healing outsustain your pokes

notes: Best find in this matchup: Mocking Shout's slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned, so the instinctive 'run away from the spinning Tryndamere' is exactly what makes it work — Vault repositions without turning and is the correct disengage. That now appears in two fields. The Bloodlust-as-W slot error survives in the mid and late paragraphs ('his W self-heal' twice); dosFull[2].t also reads 'Blind (E) his crit autos' when the blind is Q, but at 24 characters it falls under the applier's 25-character skip and needs a manual fix.
